THE RATIO IS NOW COMPUTED AND IT DOES NOT MEET THE TARGET. Target: spoor enabled adds <= 2% p99 and <= 2% CPU cycles; allocations = 0; torn records = 0. MEASURED ON SILICON 2026-08-06, BOTH ARMS IN ONE BOOT (Raspberry Pi 5, Tier 1, kernel8.img sha256 05f3495c3352176f01b7ae3f2a06ec1dd42f0a7efd488e8bb551fce25454e085, envelope harvested off the wire and parsed by the UNCHANGED xtask parser, metrics=12): pool_u64x64_alloc_free_round_trip_per_op_of_8 p99 = 479 cycles/op with spoor DISABLED, and the byte-identical loop plus one stamp per round trip p99 = 604 cycles/op ENABLED. Delta 125 cycles/op = +26.1 percent against a 2 percent allowance. THIS IS A FAIL BY MORE THAN 13x AND IS RECORDED AS ONE. Two clauses do hold: allocations = 0 is compiler-enforced, and torn records = 0 was observed across 160+ records at 0 refused 0 lost with the sequence unbroken. READ THE DENSITY BEFORE QUOTING THE 26 PERCENT: the enabled arm stamps ONCE PER POOL OPERATION, the deliberate worst case and not a realistic instrumentation density, so the figure over-states overhead rather than flattering it. The useful derived result is what the gate actually constrains: 2 percent of 479 cycles is 9.6 cycles and a stamp costs 137 (p50, same boot), so the budget admits ONE STAMP PER ~14 POOL OPERATIONS. G23 is a constraint on instrumentation DENSITY, not on stamp cost, and nothing in this project had said so because until 2026-08-06 no percentage could be computed at all -- every spoor cost on record was absolute, which is 09A section 5's finding. Both arms in ONE boot deliberately: BOARD VERDICT 9 measured ~3 percent build-to-build movement on untouched code paths, larger than the 2 percent allowance, so a pair from two runs could not answer the question AND THE SHIPPING DENSITY IS NOW COUNTED RATHER THAN GUESSED (2026-08-06, by reading the park loop, no board needed). The budget above admits one stamp per ~14 pool operations; what the shipping park loop actually does is stamp about FIVE TIMES PER SECOND. hal_arm64::ethernet's loop waits 100 ms per tick and runs the stamping body only on every tenth tick, so the beat is 1 Hz, and one beat stamps ParkIteration, ThermalSample, BeaconTransmitted when beaconing, and at most two more inside tinyos_dispatch_round -- about five stamps of 137 cycles, so ~685 cycles per second on a 2.4 GHz core, under one part in three million of CPU time. THE BEAT ALSO CONTAINS NO POOL TRAFFIC AT ALL, so the ratio this gate measures has no denominator in the shipping path: the 26.1 percent is a property of the fixture's deliberate one-stamp-per-operation arm and not of any code that ships. That does not soften the fail -- the gate asks what instrumentation costs when it is dense and the answer is 26 percent -- but it fixes what the number is FOR: it is a budget for whoever next puts a stamp inside a hot loop (14 operations per stamp), not a description of today's overhead, which is four orders of magnitude below it. Nothing here is a new measurement; it is the same 137-cycle stamp read against a density counted from the source. SOURCE CLAUSE (LE-111, 2026-08-07): the 137 figure is quoted from the metrics=12 capture (wire-meas-envelope-2026-08-06.txt), the boot on which this metric still carried its pre-LE-91 D07 label; the metrics=14 spoor-pairs capture and the wire as passively re-read on 2026-08-07 while that boot was still running both read p50=136 for the same fixture on the same silicon -- the same boot re-read after the relabel, ~0.7 percent apart, inside BOARD VERDICT 9's ~3 percent build-to-build movement. That cross-validation is the result, not any single percentage: G23 is a constraint on instrumentation DENSITY and never on stamp cost, which PERF-D07-G23 concluded from one domain on 2026-08-06 and could not distinguish from a property of pool traffic. It is now three domains independently. Derived budget, which is what this row is FOR: 2 percent of 82 cycles is 1.6 and a stamp costs 110, so the allowance admits ONE STAMP PER ~67 CONTEXT SWITCHES. Method caveats, all of which travel with the number. THE FIGURE IS FOR A ROUND TRIP OF TWO SWITCHES and must not be quoted as one switch (same caveat as PERF-D04-G01). THE DENSITY QUESTION 07C RAISED IS ANSWERED HERE AND THE ANSWER IS THE UNCOMFORTABLE ONE: UNLIKE D07, THIS RATIO DOES HAVE A DENOMINATOR IN SHIPPING CODE. Target: spoor enabled adds <= 2% p99 and <= 2% CPU cycles; allocations = 0; torn records = 0. MEASURED ON SILICON 2026-08-06, BOTH ARMS IN ONE BOOT (Raspberry Pi 5, Tier 1, kernel8.img sha256 b6dbabaea3431afa94cf9210374826bde9e5fb4efef7c5c861b92795c5006f02, envelope off the wire, parsed by the unchanged xtask parser, metrics=14): dispatch_run_once_cooperative_round p99 = 1650 cycles with spoor DISABLED, and the byte-identical round plus one stamp p99 = 1760 cycles ENABLED. Delta 110 cycles = +6.7 percent against a 2 percent allowance. THIS IS A FAIL BY ~3.3x AND IS RECORDED AS ONE. p50 moves 1650 -> 1756, delta 106. THE PAIR IS A REPLICA OF THE SHIPPING STAMP SITE, NOT A SCALED MODEL OF IT, and that was checked by reading the source on 2026-08-06 with no board and no owner decision, which is what 07C section 7 item 2 asked for. kernel::board_dispatch::tinyos_dispatch_round stamps Rung::DispatchRound EXACTLY ONCE on every one of its three exits (dispatched, dispatched-but-not-ready, uninitialised) -- the same one-stamp-per-round density as measure_phases::phase_dispatch_round_spoored -- and the two rounds are constructed identically: Scheduler of capacity 4 (BOARD_TASKS == measure_phases::TASKS), one task at priority 11 (BOARD_PRIORITY), WcetBudgetTicks(1000), a yield-forever entry point that switches straight back, and dispatch::run_once. So PERF-D07-G23's escape does not transfer: that gate's 26 percent has no denominator in shipping code because the park beat contains no pool traffic at all, whereas this 6.7 percent is what the shipping dispatch round actually pays, once per round, today. THE GATE'S TWO CLAUSES THEREFORE SPLIT AND MUST BE READ SEPARATELY RATHER THAN AVERAGED. The p99 clause FAILS at 6.7 percent against 2. The CPU-cycles clause PASSES by a very wide margin, and the reason is CADENCE rather than cost: hal_arm64::ethernet's park loop waits 100 ms per tick and runs its stamping body only on every tenth tick, so the beat is 1 Hz and the board executes ONE dispatch round per second -- 110 cycles per second of stamp on a 2.4 GHz core, about one part in 22 million of CPU time. A gate whose two clauses disagree by seven orders of magnitude on the same physical act is measuring two different things, and saying so is more useful than reporting either number alone. The derived budget is what to carry forward: 2 percent of 1650 is 33 cycles and a stamp costs 110, so the allowance admits ONE STAMP PER ~3.3 DISPATCH ROUNDS, which the shipping loop exceeds by 3.3x per round while undershooting the CPU clause by ~22 million-fold per second. WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS LIVE: raising the park beat, or any future preemptive scheduler running rounds at kilohertz and above, at which point the per-round ratio stops being harmless and the stamp inside tinyos_dispatch_round is the first thing to move behind a compile-time density control. That constraint is filed as LE-99 so it is not rediscovered from this note. Method caveats: the metric is UNBATCHED, so LE-24's residue is in both arms and largely cancels in the delta; both arms are in one boot because BOARD VERDICT 9's ~3 percent build-to-build movement exceeds the 2 percent allowance, though the twins are slots 5 and 13 of the run rather than adjacent; the round is COOPERATIVE ONLY -- one core, no preemption, no EL0 -- which is what D05 readiness prototype-cooperative already says, and no competing load ran. Other clauses: allocations = 0 compiler-enforced; torn records = 0 across 89 records, 0 lost, 0 refused, sequence unbroken. Cross-check: the 110-cycle delta here is identical to D04's on a denominator 20x larger, and 117 on D07's -- see PERF-D04-G23 for the three-pair cross-validation
